description: Single and two storey side extension; single storey rear extension; alterations and extension to roof; rear dormer; rooflights in front and side roof slopes; external alterations; change of use from dwelling (C3) to  7 bed HMO (sui generis); bin / cycle storage (demolition of detached garage and rear conservatory)
decision_conditions:
The
proposed development, by reason of the absence of information submitted to
demonstrate safe access and egress of the proposed off-street vehicle car
parking space, in conjunction with the proposed siting of the bin stores and
cycle storage to the application site’s frontage, would result in adverse
impact on highway safety in terms of occupiers’ and visitors’ unimpeded
pedestrian access to the application site and highway safety of wider
pedestrian users of the footpath along Carlton Avenue. The proposed development
is contrary to the National Planning Policy Framework (2026), Policy D3 and
Policy T4(f) of the London Plan (2021) and Policies GR1, M1 and CE1(B) of the
Harrow Local Plan (2021-2041).

<p style="text-align: justify; "><span style="font-size:11.0pt"><span style="line-height:115%">The proposed change of use of the property to a large 7-bedroom House in Multiple Occupation (HMO)(Sui Generis) would result in an intensified form of residential occupation in a location that is not considered suitable for such development. The site would have an insufficient original internal floor space below the minimum 130sqm required by Policy HO10(1) of the Harrow Local Plan (2021-2041). The site is located within a residential street characterised predominantly by family housing. The proposal therefore conflicts with criteria (1) and (3) of Policy HO10 of the Harrow Local Plan (2021-2041) which seeks to ensure the internal floorspace of the dwelling is in excess of 130sqm as originally built and to direct larger HMOs away from areas characterised by family housing.&nbsp;</span></span></p>

<p style="text-align: justify; "><span style="font-size:11pt">The proposed development, by virtue of the intensified form of residential occupation and the scale of the use and the resultant increased comings and goings, activity and general disturbance associated with the occupation of the property by up to 12no. unrelated individuals would be detrimental to the living conditions of neighbouring occupiers. The proposal is therefore contrary to the National Planning Policy Framework (2026), London Plan Policies D13 and D14, Policy GR1.C of the Harrow Local Plan (2021-2041) and Strategic Policy 01 and criterion (4) of Policy HO10 of the Harrow Local Plan (2021-2041).</span></p>

<p style="text-align: justify; "><span style="font-size:11pt">The proposed change of use to a 7-bedroom House in Multiple Occupation (Sui Generis) has failed to demonstrate that the servicing, refuse and recycling storage, cycle parking and associated hard and soft landscaping required to support the development can be accommodated within the site in a manner which would maintain an attractive frontage and preserve the character and appearance of the surrounding residential area. <span style="line-height:115%"><span arial="">Officers are not satisfied that the waste storage, as shown on the submitted proposed site plan, would be adequate in quantum to serve the proposed development. </span></span></span><span style="font-size:11.0pt">By virtue of insufficient information regarding the design, capacity and integration of this infrastructure within the site, the Local Planning Authority is unable to conclude that the proposal would provide a satisfactory design-led solution or comply with criteria (4), (8) and (10) of Policy HO10. The proposal therefore conflicts with the National Planning Policy Framework (2026), London Plan Policy D3, Strategic Policy 01 and Policies GR1, HO10(4), (8), (10) and CE1 of the Harrow Local Plan (2021-2041).</span></p>
